newsitem.title: UK: Mark crosses steady to slightly firmer in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Mark crosses steady to slightly firmer in Europe.

text.p: The mark was steady to slightly firmer on its European crosses on Thursday, shrugging off comments from Bundesbank member Reimut Jochimsen which gave a downbeat outlook on progress toward European monetary union.
Jochimsen also said late Wednesday he did not rule out another German interest rate cut in the present economic cycle but also added that he did not see one at present.
The rate cut comments briefly lifted dollar/mark, putting some pressure on the mark crosses, but dealers said they settled mainly on Jochimsen's EMU remarks.
Jochimsen warned that EMU's prospects were threatened by a lack of political integration and by fundamental dissent between France and Germany.
Analysts said concern was growing that France had little intention of taking budgetary measures to meet EMU criteria, counting on a loose interpretation of the EMU criteria for its start.
"Attempting to hit the target and failing is one thing, not bothering at all is quite another," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"Unless France can convince Germany of its sincerity, the market may soon begin to doubt Germany's recent willingness to allow a more flexible interpretation of the criteria."
Such concerns may interrupt the current cycle of EMU optimism for a timely, broad-based start, but the mark crosses have, so far, shrugged off those doubts.
Mark/French franc stood at 3.3749/54 from 3.3746/41 late Wednesday. Mark/peseta was little changed at 84.43/45.

The lira, meantime, remained firm though off Wednesday's fresh five-month high against the mark. EMU optimism as well as the growing prospect of a near-term Italian rate cut continued to buoy the lira and helped take Italian BTP futures to fresh record highs earlier.
The Italian 10-year yield spread over Germany widened slightly from Wednesday's record low of around 111 basis points but analysts still see mileage in further Italian convergence.

"The market is keeping the idea of a soft EMU at the front of its mind, which is good for Italy," said Julian Jessop, chief European economist at Nikko Europe. "There is still further to go in Italian convergence."
Mark/lira was trading at 976.25/75 from 975.70/90 late Wednesday.
Earlier today, the European Investment Bank added 250 billion lire to the one trillion lire, ten-year Euro bond announced this week. This issue can be redenominated into euros after the start of EMU.
